source: EVM-native DeFi exploits only (Ethereum, BSC, Polygon, Arbitrum, Optimism, Avalanche, Blast, Heco). Curated from Rekt, Chainalysis, Halborn, Immunefi post-mortems, and protocol disclosures. Excludes centralised exchange compromises (Bybit, DMM, WazirX, HTX, Poloniex, BitMart), wallet-drainer / phishing incidents where the root cause is user-side (Atomic Wallet), prop-trading / market-maker hot-wallet losses (Wintermute), validator-backed L1 bridge incidents where the chain itself is the target (BNB Chain hard-fork bypass), and non-EVM incidents. Bridge hacks whose EVM-side smart contract was the exploited component are included (Ronin, Nomad, Harmony, Poly, Wormhole-EVM-side excluded as Solana primary). Amounts are USD at time of exploit per the cited source.

hacks.rootCause: Five of nine Ronin validator keys compromised via social engineering of a Sky Mavis engineer; attacker forged bridge withdrawal signatures. Axie DAO allowlist had been left open from a November 2021 temporary arrangement
hacks.recoveryNote: Users made whole via Sky Mavis + Binance capital raise; on-chain funds not recovered, attributed to Lazarus Group

hacks.rootCause: EthCrossChainManager contract could call EthCrossChainData to rotate the cross-chain keeper; lax signature/type checking let the attacker set themselves as the sole keeper across Ethereum, BSC and Polygon
hacks.recoveryNote: Attacker returned all funds within two weeks, claiming white-hat intent; Poly Network offered a CSO role

hacks.rootCause: Flaw in IAVL Merkle proof verification let the attacker forge a valid proof for a withdrawal that was never committed, minting 2M BNB on BSC
hacks.recoveryNote: Validators halted BSC within 3 hours; only ~$137M escaped cross-chain, rest frozen via Moran hardfork

hacks.protocol: Wormhole (Ethereum side affected, exploit on Solana)
hacks.rootCause: Excluded from EVM top-30: root cause sat on Solana. Already counted in solana-hacks.json.
hacks.recoveryNote: Listed here only as a methodology note so readers do not double-count; skip in aggregation.

hacks.rootCause: Private key compromise added an unauthorised minter on the PLA ERC-20 contract; attacker minted 1.79B PLA across two incidents
hacks.recoveryNote: Only ~$32M of minted supply was liquidated; exchanges froze majority before conversion

hacks.rootCause: Dormant MINTER role on the GALA ERC-20 contract was accessed by an attacker; 5B GALA minted out of thin air
hacks.recoveryNote: 4.4B of 5B tokens frozen via V2 contract; attacker returned $22M in ETH from sold portion

hacks.rootCause: Cloud-provider database compromise led to hot-wallet key exposure; assets swept off the mainnet
hacks.recoveryNote: Mixin offered a $20M bounty; no material recovery reported

hacks.rootCause: Flash-loan-manipulated USDT/BNB and BUNNY/BNB pair pricing on PancakeSwap let the attacker mint ~7M BUNNY against distorted collateral, then dump
hacks.recoveryNote: BUNNY collapsed 96%; protocol issued a compensation plan but most value unrecovered

hacks.rootCause: Missing health check on the donateToReserves function let an attacker push a position into deep insolvency then self-liquidate at a profit
hacks.recoveryNote: Attacker returned all recoverable funds (~$240M at returned-date ETH prices) after negotiation

hacks.rootCause: Routine upgrade initialised the trusted Merkle root to zero; the zero root passed message verification so any arbitrary withdrawal message was accepted
hacks.recoveryNote: ~$37M returned by white-hats; bulk lost to copycat opportunists

hacks.rootCause: No execution delay on governance proposals; attacker flash-loaned $1B of stablecoins, accumulated Stalk voting power, passed a malicious BIP, and drained the reserve
hacks.recoveryNote: Funds laundered through Tornado Cash; Beanstalk relaunched with a 7-day timelock

hacks.rootCause: Proposal 62 Comptroller upgrade contained a bug that over-distributed COMP rewards; any user could call drip() to refill the reservoir
hacks.recoveryNote: ~$49M returned voluntarily by recipients; remainder permanently distributed

hacks.rootCause: Third-party wallet provider (Venly) semi-custody credentials exfiltrated for 96 user wallets, draining PYR holdings
hacks.recoveryNote: Majority of affected wallets reimbursed from treasury; team stated commitment to full reimbursement

hacks.rootCause: Flash-loan manipulation of yUSD price calculation in the yUSDVault, letting the attacker inflate crYUSD collateral value to 2x and drain the lending pool
hacks.recoveryNote: Third major Cream exploit of 2021; protocol never recovered meaningful TVL

hacks.rootCause: Rounding-direction error in the upscale function of ComposableStablePools during batchSwap; weaponised via 8-9 wei balance manipulation to corrupt the pool invariant
hacks.recoveryNote: ~$20M recovered by StakeWise and white-hats; Balancer Labs announced shutdown

hacks.rootCause: MPC keyshares held solely by CEO Zhaojun He, detained by Chinese authorities; outflows later moved by his sister for claimed asset preservation
hacks.recoveryNote: Multichain ceased operations; classified by Chainalysis as possible insider rug rather than external exploit

hacks.rootCause: Compromised Cloudflare API key injected malicious JS into the Badger front-end, silently inserting unlimited-approval txs into user wallets
hacks.recoveryNote: Some funds recovered via CEX cooperation; BadgerDAO covered remainder from treasury

hacks.rootCause: Permissionless updatePrice function on the Tellor-backed oracle let the attacker pump then crash the WALBT price, minting BEUR and mass-liquidating troves
hacks.recoveryNote: Most BEUR was illiquid; AllianceBlock minted replacement ALBT for affected holders

hacks.rootCause: Excluded from EVM top-30: native Solana protocol, already counted in solana-hacks.json.
hacks.recoveryNote: Reference only.

hacks.rootCause: 2-of-5 multisig on the Horizon bridge; two signer keys compromised, attributed by FBI to Lazarus Group
hacks.recoveryNote: Funds laundered through Tornado Cash; Harmony network economy permanently damaged

hacks.rootCause: Legacy deposit function left in QBridge after migration to depositETH; attacker passed a zero-address sentinel to mint qXETH without depositing WETH
hacks.recoveryNote: Protocol effectively defunct; $250k bounty offer ignored

hacks.rootCause: Seven of ten multisig signers compromised on the Ethereum vault contract; ETH and DAI drained in a single block
hacks.recoveryNote: Orbit working with law enforcement; attacker funded from Tornado Cash

hacks.rootCause: Vyper compiler versions 0.2.15, 0.2.16 and 0.3.0 mis-compiled the @nonreentrant decorator, leaving several Curve pools reentrant on add_liquidity/remove_liquidity
hacks.recoveryNote: ~$52M recovered via white-hats and attacker negotiations; net loss ~$20M

hacks.rootCause: Rogue developer retained ownership of the upgradeable proxy deployer; upgraded contract to a malicious implementation and swept user ETH
hacks.recoveryNote: Developer returned all private keys after 1h negotiation; no user loss

hacks.rootCause: INLETDRIFT macOS malware delivered via a fake contractor PDF compromised three multisig signers; blind-signing allowed a malicious transferOwnership tx to pass manual review
hacks.recoveryNote: Attribution to DPRK UNC4736 (AppleJeus/Citrine Sleet) by Mandiant

hacks.rootCause: Precision error at tick-interval boundaries in concentrated liquidity maths; attacker double-counted liquidity and drained pools across five chains
hacks.recoveryNote: ~$5M recovered via frontrunner bot negotiations; treasury grant plan for affected users

hacks.rootCause: Unreleased HomoraBankv2 pool with uninitialised state let the attacker lend and borrow sUSD repeatedly via flash loans to accumulate cySUSD and drain Iron Bank
hacks.recoveryNote: Alpha agreed to divert 20% of protocol fees + 50M ALPHA collateral; years-long repayment dispute with Iron Bank

hacks.rootCause: Missing reentrancy guard on batchHarvestMarketRewards let an attacker register a malicious Pendle SY market and inflate reward accounting via mid-call deposits
hacks.recoveryNote: Attacker ignored bounty offer; laundered via Tornado Cash

hacks.rootCause: Aave flash loan imbalanced Curve 3CRV pool; v1 yDAI vault was forced to deposit at unfavourable rate via permissionless earn(), then rebalance reversed
hacks.recoveryNote: Yearn treasury minted DAI via a Maker vault to make depositors whole

hacks.rootCause: repayForAll in CauldronV4 cleared elastic but not base in the debt accounting, letting the attacker rebase part to an arbitrary value and mint MIM
hacks.recoveryNote: MIM depegged briefly to $0.77; attacker funded via Tornado Cash

hacks.rootCause: Compound-fork empty-market donation attack: attacker donated WBTC to an unused hWBTC market with zero supply, inflating the exchange rate, then redeemed with rounding-favour
hacks.recoveryNote: Protocol did not recover; same vulnerability pattern hit multiple Compound forks

hacks.rootCause: Input validation failure in CorkHook contract allowed deployment of fake token contracts to manipulate exchange rate calculations via beforeSwap function; affected code was outside original audit scope
hacks.recoveryNote: Stolen funds remained in attacker wallet at time of disclosure

hacks.rootCause: ERC4626 donation attack on freshly deployed, under-collateralised vault: attacker donated 2000 crvUSD to inflate share price, minted 1 wei of shares, then borrowed against worthless collateral after oracle rounding eliminated borrowing restrictions
hacks.recoveryNote: $2.8M repaid toward $9.5M user loss ($1.4M from C2tP, $810K from Convex, $600K initial treasury)

hacks.rootCause: Cross-contract reentrancy vulnerability in executeDecreaseOrder function; malicious contract callback manipulated global short average prices, inflating GLP pricing to enable arbitrary mint/redemption cycles
hacks.recoveryNote: $37M returned to GMX Security Multisig after $5M white-hat bounty paid; coordinated vulnerability disclosure rather than a malicious attack

hacks.rootCause: Precision bug in custom Liquidity Distribution Function: carefully-sized trades broke the rebalancing math, allowing repeated withdrawals of more tokens than deserved through rounding errors
hacks.recoveryNote: Funds bridged to Ethereum in 100 ETH chunks via Across Protocol; Cyfrin audit in June 2025 had flagged precision risk

hacks.rootCause: Multisig administrator compromised delegateCall function to remove existing admins and install themselves as sole owner; drained treasury and minted ~10 trillion UXLINK tokens across Ethereum, Arbitrum and BSC
hacks.recoveryNote: Token swap to new Ethereum contract with 1B hard cap and removed mint function; potential user compensation contingent on laundering trail recovery

hacks.rootCause: Unchecked integer overflow in getPurchasePrice() function; contract deployed in Solidity 0.5.3 without SafeMath protection, allowing attacker to input large values that wrapped to near-zero and mint billions of tokens for effectively free
hacks.recoveryNote: Entire 8,535 ETH deposited into Tornado Cash by Jan 10; no compensation figures announced

hacks.rootCause: CAPO (Correlated Asset Price Oracle) configuration mismatch with stale anchor ratio; rate-limiter capped a legitimate ratio update 2.85% below market, triggering liquidations on leveraged E-Mode positions that were healthy in reality
hacks.recoveryNote: Aave DAO approved 512 ETH reimbursement of affected users; net treasury cost 357 ETH after Titan Builder returns (142 ETH) and liquidation fees (13 ETH). Classified here for methodology alignment though this was a liquidation event, not a drain

hacks.rootCause: Supply-chain attack: compromised GitHub credential from a third-party project where a Resolv contractor had worked; attacker deployed malicious CI/CD workflow to exfiltrate cloud infrastructure credentials, escalated to SERVICE_ROLE key controlling USR minting, minted 80M unbacked USR
hacks.recoveryNote: 46M of 80M illicit USR removed from circulation via redemptions and burns; downstream debt cleared at partner protocols (Fluid $70M, Venus $31.6M, Lista $8.4M); attacker's ~$25M in ETH remains at large

hacks.rootCause: LayerZero bridge verifier compromised via server-level poisoning of a 1-of-1 validator configuration; attacker minted ~116,500 unbacked rsETH tokens (~18% of circulating supply) across 20+ chains, primarily Ethereum and Arbitrum. LayerZero preliminary analysis attributes to a state actor (likely Lazarus Group)
hacks.recoveryNote: Emergency freezes activated across Aave V3, Aave V4, SparkLend, Fluid, and other platforms. Arbitrum Security Council placed approximately $71M in frozen assets in governance-controlled wallets. Cascade losses of $123-230M estimated across downstream DeFi protocols

hacks.rootCause: Reentrancy attack on the splitDAO function: withdrawal was processed before the balance was updated, allowing repeated withdrawals from a single deposit. 3.6M ETH drained to a child DAO
hacks.recoveryNote: Ethereum hard fork at block 1,920,000 restored funds to investors; the un-forked chain (Ethereum Classic) kept the original history with the theft intact

hacks.rootCause: Parity wallet library contract was not initialized; a user triggered initWallet to take ownership, then called the kill function, permanently suicide-ing the shared library and freezing approximately 513k ETH across 600+ multisig wallets that depended on it
hacks.recoveryNote: Funds are permanently locked on-chain rather than stolen; EIP-156 and EIP-867 proposed recovery mechanisms but none were adopted

hacks.rootCause: ERC-777 reentrancy via imBTC token: the token used a tokensToSend callback hook, allowing the attacker to reenter the lendf.me supply function and inflate their apparent collateral
hacks.recoveryNote: Attacker returned all funds after their IP metadata was linked to identifying information; funds returned within 3 days

hacks.rootCause: Unfinished Andre Cronje test contracts were discovered and flashloan-attacked by a user who minted EMN tokens, then drained the bonding curve reserves
hacks.recoveryNote: Attacker returned $8M to Andre Cronje for user reimbursement; remaining funds kept

hacks.rootCause: Flashloan price oracle manipulation on the Curve Y pool, arbitraging the inflated USDC and USDT price against Harvest's fUSDC and fUSDT vaults
hacks.recoveryNote: Attacker returned approximately $2.5M; remaining funds laundered via Tornado Cash

hacks.rootCause: Flashloan reentrancy attack on the dForce savings pool in Akropolis Delphi; attacker exploited a reentrancy path to mint excess pool tokens against a single deposit
hacks.recoveryNote: Team pledged full user reimbursement from treasury and insurance reserves

hacks.rootCause: Flashloan price oracle manipulation on the MultiStables vault: attacker manipulated Curve pool prices within the same transaction to enable favourable withdrawal from the vault
hacks.recoveryNote: Attacker returned $2M voluntarily; remainder kept

hacks.rootCause: Flashloan reentrancy on OUSD mint function: attacker supplied fake collateral then reentered before the mint accounting updated, inflating their OUSD balance
hacks.recoveryNote: Team pledged reimbursement via OGN token rewards rather than direct fund recovery

hacks.rootCause: Vault swap exploit: attacker deployed a malicious evil jar and exploited the transferProtocolFees function to swap Pickle Finance DAI deposits into the attacker's fake jar without proper validation
hacks.recoveryNote: Pickle merged with Yearn Finance shortly afterwards; no direct recovery

hacks.rootCause: Developer rugpull: admin keys retained privileged access to swap strategies; team replaced legitimate strategy contracts with malicious ones that transferred deposits to developer-controlled wallets
hacks.recoveryNote: Developer identified as COMP.FI team and disappeared; no recovery

hacks.rootCause: Flashloan price oracle manipulation on Uniswap LP token valuation: attacker skewed Uniswap pool to inflate LP token collateral value, then borrowed against it and walked away
hacks.recoveryNote: Approximately $5.5M recovered via emergency freeze and partial attacker return

hacks.rootCause: Infinite COVER token mint via shield mining bug: the reward multiplier was incorrectly tracked across deposits and withdrawals, letting the attacker mint trillions of COVER tokens
hacks.recoveryNote: Grap Finance whitehat returned $4.4M; Binance credited users to cover the remainder; new COVER token minted to replace diluted supply
